description: Errors found by the scanner while breaking the text into tokens (characters, numbers, strings, comments).

rules.title: Character that is not part of C/C++
patterns: ^character <U\+(?P<code>[0-9A-Fa-f]+)> not allowed (?:in an identifier|at the start of an identifier)$
^non-ASCII characters are not allowed outside of literals and identifiers$
^treating Unicode character <U\+(?P<code>[0-9A-Fa-f]+)> as (?:an )?identifier character rather than as '(?P<ascii>.)' symbol$
rules.what: Line {line} contains a character that is not part of the C/C++ language: {shown}.
why: Code copied from a PDF, Word file, WhatsApp or a website often contains curly 'smart' quotes, long dashes or invisible non-breaking spaces.
A typing mistake produced a symbol that C does not use, such as `@`.
fix: Delete the marked characters and retype them with your keyboard (normal `"`, `'`, `-` and spaces).
When copying code, paste it into a plain-text editor first or switch off 'smart quotes'.
rules.tip: One wrong character usually produces several errors on the same line (undeclared names, missing brackets). Fix the character and they all go away.

rules.title: String or character never closed
rules.what: A {kind} starts with `{quote}` on line {line} but the closing `{quote}` is missing, so the compiler swallowed the rest of the line.
why: A quote inside the text was not escaped, e.g. `"He said "hi""` (write `\"` inside strings).
fix: Add the closing `{quote}` at the end of the text.
rules.tip: The errors on the following lines (expected expression, expected ';') are side effects of this one.

rules.title: Invalid number (letters stuck to a number)
rules.what: The scanner read `{number}` as one number, but `{suffix}` is not a valid ending for a number.
why: Maths-style multiplication such as `2x` (C needs `2 * x`).
A variable name that starts with a digit, such as `1stNumber` - names must start with a letter or `_`.
fix: Or rename the variable so it starts with a letter: `number1`.

rules.title: Number with a leading zero (octal)
rules.what: In C/C++ a number that starts with `0` is written in OCTAL (base 8), which only uses the digits 0-7. So `{number}` is not a valid number because it contains `{digit}`.
why: Writing dates or months with a leading zero (`08`, `09`), or padding numbers with zeros.
fix: Remove the leading zero: write `{fixed_number}` instead of `{number}`.
rules.tip: Even without an error, `010` means eight, not ten!

rules.title: Unknown escape sequence in a string
rules.what: Inside a string, a backslash `\` starts a special code like `\n` (new line) or `\t` (tab). `\{esc}` is not one of these codes.
why: A Windows path written with single backslashes, e.g. `"C:\data"`.
You wanted to print a backslash itself.
fix: To print one backslash write two: `\\`.
For file paths you can also use forward slashes: `"C:/data/file.txt"`.

rules.title: Comment never closed
rules.what: A comment started with `/*` on line {line} but there is no `*/` to end it, so the rest of your file became part of the comment.
why: The closing `*/` was forgotten or typed as `/*` again.
fix: Add `*/` where the comment should end (usually at the end of line {line}).

example.wrong:
/* calculate the sum
int sum = a + b;
example.right:
/* calculate the sum */
int sum = a + b;

rules.tip: For one-line comments `//` is safer - it ends automatically at the end of the line.

rules.title: Several characters inside single quotes
patterns: ^character constant too long for its type$
rules.what: Single quotes `' '` hold exactly ONE character, like `'a'`. `{literal}` has more than one character inside.
why: Text (a string) written with single quotes instead of double quotes.
A typo such as `'/n'` instead of `'\n'`.
fix: For a single character keep one character: `'y'`.
samples: character constant too long for its type

rules.title: Empty character constant
rules.what: `''` (two single quotes with nothing between them) is not a valid character - a character constant must contain exactly one character.
why: You wanted a space `' '`, the null character `'\0'`, or an empty string `""`.
fix: Use `' '` for a space, `'\0'` for the null character, or `""` for an empty string.
